L: The flight to San Antonio leaves at fourteen fifteen, not at four fifteen.
o: At 2:15 in the afternoon
At 4:15 in the afternoon
At 4:50 in the morning
At 2:50 in the afternoon
items.e: In military time, fourteen fifteen (1415) is 2:15 p.m. The speaker corrects the mistake "four fifteen".

L: I think the new schedule is much better.
o: She completely agrees with the man.
She does not agree with the man.
She wants a new schedule.
She cannot read the schedule.
items.e: "I couldn't agree more" means "I agree completely."

L: It's supposed to be cold and windy this afternoon, so bring your field jacket.
o: Bring warm clothing.
Stay inside all afternoon.
Bring an umbrella.
Wear light clothing.
items.e: Cold and windy weather: the speaker tells the listener to bring a field jacket, which is warm clothing.

L: I can't find the keys to the supply room.
Did you check the drawer of my desk? I usually leave them there.
items.q: Where does the woman usually leave the keys?
o: In her desk drawer
In the supply room
On top of her desk
With the man
items.e: She says "the drawer of my desk".

L: Did you make it to the finance office before it closed?
o: Yes, with ten minutes to spare.
Yes, I made it myself.
It closes at five on weekdays.
About two hundred dollars.
items.e: Here "make it" means "get there in time". "Yes, with ten minutes to spare" means the person answering got there ten minutes before the office closed.

L: Do I need an appointment for sick call, or can I just walk in?
o: You can just walk in, but get there early.
I walked there yesterday afternoon.
Yes, I feel much better now.
It was a very short appointment.
items.e: The woman asks about two choices, an appointment or "just walk in". The best reply picks one of them: she can just walk in.

L: You must wear hearing protection in the generator room, even if you're only going in for a minute.
items.q: When must people wear hearing protection in the generator room?
o: Every single time they go in
Only when they stay a long time
Only during their first minute inside
Only when a generator is being repaired
items.e: "Even if you're only going in for a minute" means there is no exception. Hearing protection is needed every time.

L: Unless you score at least seventy on the progress test, you'll have to repeat the unit.
items.q: What will happen to a student who scores 65?
o: The student will repeat the unit.
The student will go on to the next unit.
The student will leave the school.
The student will change instructors.
items.e: "Unless you score at least seventy" means "if you score less than seventy". Sixty-five is less than seventy, so the student must repeat the unit.

L: Excuse me, is this the gate for flight five eighteen to Denver?
o: No, that flight leaves from Gate 12.
It lands at 5:18.
I've been to Denver twice.
It takes about two hours.
items.e: The man asks if he is at the right gate. Only "No, that flight leaves from Gate 12" answers that question.

L: Do you know if the new printer in the orderly room works yet?
It works, all right, as long as you only need one page at a time.
items.q: What does the woman imply about the printer?
o: It has trouble with longer documents.
It has not been installed yet.
It only prints in black and white for now.
It is faster than the old one.
items.e: "As long as you only need one page" suggests it fails with bigger print jobs.

L: Is the colonel in a good mood today?
I'd stay out of her way if I were you.
o: The colonel is in a bad mood.
The colonel is very happy.
The colonel is on vacation.
The colonel wants to see her.
items.e: His advice suggests a bad mood.

L: Did you send the training schedule to the battalion yet?
It's ready to go, but the operations officer asked for one more change before it goes out.
items.q: Why hasn't the schedule been sent?
o: It still needs to be revised.
The battalion already has a copy.
The operations officer lost it.
Nobody has typed it up yet.
items.e: The operations officer wants another change made before it is sent.

L: Can you finish the job by Friday?
I'll do my best, but no promises.
o: He will try but isn't sure.
He will surely finish.
He refuses the job.
He finished already.
items.e: He commits to trying, not to the deadline.

L: Do you have this shirt in a medium?
Let me check in the back.
items.q: What will the woman probably do?
o: Look for the shirt in the storeroom
Give him a large shirt
Close the store
Call another store
items.e: "Check in the back" means look in the storeroom.

L: Put the boxes in the corner, please.
Do you want them stacked or side by side?
items.q: What is the woman going to do?
o: Move some boxes
Open the boxes
Buy more boxes
Throw the boxes away
items.e: She is about to place the boxes.

L: The motor sergeant wants all drivers to do their vehicle checks before the convoy leaves.
That's going to be tight. We roll out at zero six hundred, and half the trucks are still covered in ice.
o: The checks may not get done in time.
Half the drivers will miss the convoy.
The convoy leaves at six in the evening.
The checks were finished last night.
items.e: "Tight" means there is barely enough time, especially with icy trucks.

L: My essay is due tomorrow, and I haven't started.
You'd better get to work right now.
o: Starting the essay immediately
Asking for more time
Copying an essay
Going to bed
items.e: She advises starting now.

L: Do you think the colonel will like the plan?
I doubt it; it's too expensive.
o: The colonel will not like it.
The colonel will love it.
The plan is too cheap.
The colonel hasn't seen it.
items.e: "I doubt it" means probably not.

L: I think the meeting was a waste of time.
o: She thinks it was useless too.
She disagrees with the man.
She found the meeting very useful.
She thinks the meeting was too long.
items.e: "I couldn't agree more" means she agrees completely that the meeting was pointless.

L: Is Lieutenant Harris in her office?
She just left for lunch; she'll be back at one.
items.q: When will Lieutenant Harris be back?
o: At noon
In ten minutes
Tomorrow
items.e: She returns at one.

L: How long will the repairs take?
Two days for the parts and one day to install them.
items.q: How long will the repairs take in all?
o: Three days
Two days
One day
Four days
items.e: Two days plus one day equals three days.

L: Why didn't you answer my e-mail?
It went into my junk folder by mistake.
o: He didn't see the e-mail.
He was too busy.
He was angry.
He has no computer.
items.e: It went to his junk folder.

L: Why don't you want to go to the beach?
I burn easily in the sun.
items.q: Why doesn't the woman want to go?
o: She gets sunburned easily.
She can't swim.
The water is cold.
She is busy.
items.e: She burns easily.

L: Why do you need a new uniform?
I've gained weight since the last one.
items.q: Why does the man need a new uniform?
o: His old one is too small now.
His old one was torn.
He lost it.
He got promoted.
items.e: Weight gain made it too tight.

L: Ma'am, may I have Friday off?
Only if Corporal Tate can cover your shift.
o: He can have Friday off if someone covers for him.
He can't have Friday off.
He must work two shifts.
Corporal Tate is off on Friday.
items.e: Permission depends on coverage.

L: The copier on the second floor is broken.
Use the one in the operations office.
o: Using another copier
Calling a technician
Making copies tomorrow
Buying a copier
items.e: She points to another copier.

L: Can I take the jeep to the airfield?
Take the van; the jeep's in the shop.
items.q: What does the man tell the woman?
o: Use the van instead
Walk to the airfield
Wait for the jeep
Take a taxi
items.e: The jeep is being repaired.

L: A civilian contractor from the company that makes the radios.
items.q: What do we learn about the instructor?
o: The instructor works for the radio maker.
The instructor is a soldier in the company.
The instructor repairs radios for the army.
The instructor sells radios on the base.
items.e: The teacher is a civilian employed by the company that makes the radios.

L: Can you pick up the kids at three?
I have a meeting until four. Can your mother do it?
o: The woman's mother could pick up the kids
He will leave the meeting early
The kids can walk home
The woman should pick them up at four
items.e: He can't, so he suggests her mother.

L: The children are making a lot of noise.
They're excited about the trip tomorrow.
o: They are excited about a trip.
They are fighting.
They are hungry.
They are playing a game.
items.e: Excitement about the trip.

L: Give me five more minutes to finish my makeup.
o: She isn't quite ready yet.
She finished getting ready five minutes ago.
She wants to leave in fifteen minutes.
She's ready to go right now.
items.e: She needs five more minutes, so she is not ready to leave yet.

L: My daughter got the lead in the school play.
o: She is happy for him.
She is jealous.
She doesn't care.
She is worried.
items.e: "That's wonderful" shows happiness.

L: Do you know whether the land navigation course is still on for tomorrow morning?
o: As far as I know, nothing has changed.
It's still on the table by the door.
I'd rather go tomorrow afternoon.
The course covers about six kilometers.
items.e: She means the course has not been canceled, so it is still on.

L: Did anyone tell you what time the mission briefing starts tomorrow?
o: I heard seven, but check the board.
I told him all about it yesterday.
It lasted about two hours last time.
The mission went better than expected.
items.e: She gives the time she heard and suggests checking the board to be sure.

L: Who's going to give the safety briefing if the lieutenant isn't back in time?
o: Sergeant Kim offered to cover it.
He should be back by about noon.
The last one was pretty short.
I'm on my way to the safety office.
items.e: Sergeant Kim offering to cover it names the person who will give the briefing.

L: How come the briefing ran so long? It was only supposed to take twenty minutes.
o: The colonel kept asking questions.
I ran about two miles in twenty minutes.
I came as quickly as I could.
It's supposed to rain all week.
items.e: The colonel's many questions explain why the briefing took longer than planned.

L: Who's the tall man next to the window?
o: He's the new chaplain.
He's very tall.
He's looking outside.
He's waiting.
items.e: "Who" asks for identity.

L: How about going for a run after work?
o: Sounds good. What time?
I ran yesterday.
About three miles.
After work is five.
items.e: "How about" is a suggestion.

L: Was the weather briefing any good, or was it the same old forecast?
o: Nothing we didn't hear yesterday.
It was good to see you again.
The weather was awful last weekend.
She's about the same age as me.
items.e: Saying it held nothing new means it was the same old forecast.

L: Mind if I turn on the air conditioner?
o: Not at all; it's really hot.
Yes, it's an air conditioner.
It was on yesterday.
I turned it.
items.e: "Not at all" means go ahead.

L: Do you mind if I bring a friend to the party?
o: Not at all. The more, the merrier.
Yes, the party is fun.
My friend is coming.
I don't mind parties.
items.e: "The more, the merrier" welcomes extra guests.

L: Do the cooks have to go through the weapons refresher training too, or just the infantry?
o: Everyone has to, whatever their job.
The cook's been through a lot lately.
A cold drink would be refreshing.
Just the two of us went.
items.e: "Everyone, whatever their job" means the cooks must take the training too.

L: Would you like to order now or wait for your friend?
o: I'll wait for my friend, thanks.
My friend is late.
I ordered yesterday.
I'd like a friend.
items.e: The reply chooses one option.

L: Let's push the briefing back an hour. The slides still aren't finished.
o: Okay, I'll let everyone know.
I pushed the door, but it was locked.
I'll be back in about an hour.
The kids love the slide at the park.
items.e: She agrees to the delay and will tell the others about the new time.

L: What's wrong with the radio? All I'm getting is static on every channel.
o: Maybe the antenna came loose.
I'll get ready in a minute.
There's nothing wrong with me.
It's on channel five every night.
items.e: A loose antenna is a likely cause of the static.

L: Didn't the sergeant say to meet at the gym?
o: No, he said at the motor pool.
The gym is open until ten at night.
The sergeant goes to the gym every day.
We met at the gym last week.
items.e: The answer corrects him.

L: How many soldiers from our company made it through the air assault course?
o: Only three of the ten who started.
We made it home around midnight.
The air is really dry today.
Our company has about a hundred people.
items.e: Only three soldiers finished the course.

L: Is there a gas station on the way?
o: There's one just before the highway.
Gas is expensive this month.
My car uses a lot of gas.
The highway is very busy.
items.e: The answer gives the location.

L: Why was the safety briefing moved from Wednesday to Thursday afternoon?
o: The speaker couldn't make it on Wednesday.
It was very safe, thanks.
On Thursday at two o'clock, in the main conference room.
I moved here in March.
items.e: The reply gives the reason for the change: the speaker was not available.

L: Why does the check-engine light keep coming on in the staff car?
o: No idea. Let's have someone look at it.
I'll check the lights in the staff office.
It came on at about ten this morning.
Yes, the staff car is parked out back.
items.e: The speaker doesn't know the reason and suggests having the car checked.

L: Where do we meet for the road march?
o: At the north end of the parade field.
The road march is twelve miles.
We'll carry full packs.
The road march starts at five.
items.e: "Where" asks for a place.

L: Can you take the night shift on Friday?
o: I can, but I'll need Saturday off.
The night shift is very quiet.
I worked the night shift last week.
Friday is the end of the week.
items.e: The answer agrees with a condition.

L: Did the dentist say whether you'll need to come back for another visit?
o: Only for a cleaning in six months.
I visited my aunt last month.
Yes, he said hello to you.
I'll come back right after lunch.
items.e: The next visit is just a routine cleaning six months from now.

L: Which is cheaper, the bus or the train?
o: The bus, but it takes longer.
The train leaves every hour.
I take the bus every day.
The bus station is downtown.
items.e: "Which" asks for a comparison.

L: Have you gotten your annual physical yet, or is it scheduled for later this month?
o: I took care of it last week.
I do physical training every morning.
It's scheduled to rain later.
I'll get it for you.
items.e: "Took care of it" means the physical is already done.

L: What's the weather like in Seattle in winter?
o: Cool and rainy.
Seattle is in Washington State.
I visited Seattle in May.
Seattle has a big port.
items.e: The question asks for a description.

L: Which color do you prefer, blue or green?
o: Blue, I think.
Colors are important.
I like many colors.
My car is red.
items.e: "Which" asks for a choice.

L: How do you say "thank you" in Spanish?
o: "Gracias."
I speak a little Spanish.
Spanish is easy.
I learned Spanish in school.
items.e: The question asks for a translation.

L: Hello, I'm returning a call from this number. Did somebody here try to reach me?
o: That may have been my roommate. Hold on.
I'll be back in the office at three.
Yes, I can reach the top shelf.
The number is on the back of the card.
items.e: The speaker offers a likely person who called and asks the caller to wait while checking.

L: Would you be interested in joining our bowling league on Thursday nights?
o: I'd love to, but I work late on Thursdays.
I joined the Army in two thousand ten.
The bowling alley is next to the gym.
Yes, it's a very interesting story.
items.e: This is a polite refusal: the person wants to join but is working on that night.

L: Who ended up winning the volleyball tournament on Saturday?
o: The cooks, believe it or not.
It ended at about six o'clock.
On the beach behind the club.
I won't be playing this year.
items.e: The question asks who won, and the reply names the winning team: the cooks.

L: How many tickets should I get for the hockey game Friday night?
o: One for everyone except Dan. He's working.
I got mine at the gate last time.
They're twenty dollars apiece.
On Friday night at seven.
items.e: The reply tells how many to buy without giving a number: everyone in the group except Dan.

L: How's the new gym working out for you? Is it worth the membership fee?
o: Definitely. I go almost every day.
It worked out fine in the end.
You pay it at the front desk.
It's on the corner of Fifth and Main.
items.e: The person says the gym is worth the money because they use it nearly every day.

L: Formation is at zero six thirty, so we have to be on the field by six twenty.
items.q: When must they be on the field?
items.e: Formation is at 0630, but they must arrive ten minutes earlier, at 6:20.

L: I'll be on leave from the third to the seventeenth of June.
o: On June 17
On June 3
On June 7
On July 17
items.e: The leave runs from June 3 to June 17.

L: My rent went up from nine hundred to nine hundred fifty dollars a month.
items.q: How much is the rent now?
o: $950 a month
$900 a month
$50 a month
$1,950 a month
items.e: The rent increased by fifty dollars, to nine hundred fifty.

L: The doctor told me to take one tablet every six hours.
items.q: How many tablets will she take in a day?
o: Four
Six
Two
Three
items.e: There are twenty-four hours in a day: 24 divided by 6 is 4.

L: There were thirty people at the briefing yesterday and thirteen today.
items.e: Thirteen came today; thirty came yesterday.

L: The meeting was scheduled for an hour, but it lasted ninety minutes.
items.q: How much longer than planned was the meeting?
o: 30 minutes
90 minutes
One hour
10 minutes
items.e: Ninety minutes minus sixty minutes is thirty minutes.

L: The coffee here is not as strong as the coffee at the dining facility.
o: The mess hall serves stronger coffee.
The coffee here is too strong for him.
Both places serve equally strong coffee.
The dining facility has run out of coffee.
items.e: "Not as strong as" means the coffee at the dining facility (the mess hall) is stronger.

L: The left lane is closed, so all traffic must use the right lane.
items.q: What does the woman say about the road?
o: Drivers have to keep right.
Drivers have to keep left.
Drivers may use either lane.
The right lane is closed to traffic.
items.e: The left lane is closed, so everyone must stay in the right lane.

L: The repairs will be finished in a week at the earliest.
items.q: When will the repairs be finished?
o: In one week or later
In less than a week
Today
They are already finished.
items.e: "At the earliest" means not before one week.

L: Corporal Smith is not only a good mechanic but also an excellent driver.
items.q: What is true about Corporal Smith?
o: He is good at two things.
He is only a mechanic.
He cannot drive.
He is a poor mechanic.
items.e: "Not only ... but also" adds a second quality.

L: My uncle is the oldest person in our family, and he still runs every morning.
items.q: What is true about his uncle?
o: He is old but very active.
He is young.
He cannot walk.
He runs in the evening.
items.e: The oldest person still runs every morning.

L: The commander wants the report on her desk first thing tomorrow morning.
items.q: When does the commander want the report?
o: Early tomorrow morning
Tonight
Tomorrow afternoon
Next week
items.e: "First thing tomorrow morning" means very early tomorrow.

L: The lieutenant asked me to make twenty copies of the training schedule.
items.q: What did the lieutenant ask for?
o: Copies of the schedule
A new schedule
Twenty training sessions
A meeting
items.e: He must make twenty copies.

L: The sergeant major will inspect the barracks at ten instead of at nine.
items.q: What has changed about the inspection?
o: It will be an hour later.
It will start at nine.
It has been canceled.
It will last from nine to ten.
items.e: It moved from nine to ten, one hour later.

L: I asked for a transfer to Germany, but they sent me to Korea.
o: He did not get his first choice.
He was sent to Germany as he asked.
He asked to go to Korea.
He is still waiting for a transfer.
items.e: He asked for Germany but was sent to Korea instead.

L: You can pick up your new ID card at the personnel office after three.
items.q: When can he pick up the ID card?
o: After three o'clock
Before three o'clock
Tomorrow
Next week
items.e: The card is ready after three.

L: Turn left at the second traffic light, and the clinic is on your right.
o: After the second light, on the right
After the first light, on the left
Before the second light
Next to the first light
items.e: Left at the second light, then on the right.

L: The bus terminal is three blocks north of the train station.
o: Three blocks north of the station
Three blocks south of the station
Next to the station
Inside the station
items.e: It is three blocks north.

L: Hurricane season starts in June, so we keep extra water and batteries at home.
items.q: Why do they keep supplies at home?
o: To be ready for hurricanes
To save money
Because stores close in June
For a party
items.e: They prepare for hurricane season.

L: The heat wave is expected to last until the end of the week.
o: It will stay hot for the rest of the week.
The heat wave ended at the end of last week.
The heat wave will last for several weeks.
It will be cooler by the middle of the week.
items.e: The heat wave is expected to continue until the end of the week.

L: I lost my wallet on the train, but someone turned it in to the lost and found.
o: Someone returned it.
It was stolen.
He found it at home.
It is still missing.
items.e: "Turned it in" means gave it to the lost and found.

L: I can't go swimming today because I have an ear infection.
o: She has an ear infection.
The pool is closed.
It's too cold.
She can't swim.
items.e: An ear infection keeps her out of the water.

L: I'm saving money to buy a car, so I don't go out much these days.
items.q: Why doesn't he go out much?
o: He is saving for a car.
He doesn't have any friends.
He is studying for exams.
His car is being repaired.
items.e: He is saving money.

L: My wife works downtown, so she takes the train instead of driving.
items.q: Why does his wife take the train?
o: She works in the city center.
She doesn't have a driver's license.
The train is cheaper than gas.
She likes to read on the train.
items.e: Working downtown is the reason.

L: My family is coming to visit for the holidays, so I took two weeks off.
items.q: Why did he take time off?
o: His family is visiting.
He is sick.
He is moving.
He is going on a trip.
items.e: He wants time with his family.

L: The hardware store gave me the wrong size of screws, so I have to go back.
items.q: Why does he have to go back?
o: He got the wrong screws.
He forgot his receipt.
The store called him.
He needs more paint.
items.e: The screws were the wrong size.

L: I always check the price per ounce to find the best deal.
items.q: What does he do when he shops?
o: Compares prices carefully
Buys the biggest package
Buys only on sale days
Uses coupons only
items.e: Price per ounce helps compare.

L: The flight school accepts only twenty students a year, so it's very competitive.
items.q: Why is the flight school competitive?
o: It accepts very few students.
Its courses are very expensive.
Its instructors are very strict.
Its classes are very long.
items.e: Few places make it hard to get in.

L: Trainees may call home on Sundays between two and four in the afternoon.
o: Sunday afternoons, 2 to 4
Every evening
Saturday mornings
Any time on Sunday
items.e: Calls are allowed Sunday 2 to 4 p.m.

L: The tactics class was so interesting that nobody noticed the time.
o: The class was very interesting.
The class was boring.
The class was too long.
Nobody came to class.
items.e: Time passed quickly because it was interesting.

L: The barber shop on base used to open every day, but since the new manager arrived, it's closed on Sundays and Mondays.
items.q: How many days a week is the barber shop open now?
o: Five
Seven
Six
Two
items.e: It is now closed two days a week, so it is open on the other five.

L: I thought the driving test would be a breeze, but the instructor made me parallel park three times before he passed me.
items.q: What can be concluded about the man's driving test?
o: It was more difficult than he expected.
It was exactly as easy as he had expected.
He had to take it three different times.
The instructor refused to let him pass.
items.e: He expected an easy test, but he had to repeat the parking several times before he passed.

L: I'm afraid I've bitten off more than I can chew with this job.
o: He took on too much work.
He ate too much at lunch.
He hurt his teeth.
He doesn't have enough work.
items.e: It means accepting more than you can handle.

L: The news about the base closing came out of the blue.
o: The news was unexpected.
The news was expected.
The news was about the sky.
The news was sad.
items.e: "Out of the blue" means without warning.

L: We're running short on time, so let's get to the point.
o: To focus on the main issue
To run outside
To take a break
To start over
items.e: "Get to the point" means talk about the main thing.

L: I have a bone to pick with you about the car.
o: He wants to complain to her.
He wants to share a meal.
He wants to give her a gift.
He agrees with her.
items.e: "A bone to pick" means a complaint.

L: Most of the snow melted yesterday, but the roads are still slippery.
o: Drivers should still be careful.
The roads are covered with deep snow.
More snow is expected tomorrow.
The roads are dry and safe again.
items.e: The snow has mostly melted, but slippery roads mean drivers still need to be careful.

L: The fire department visits the school every year to teach safety.
items.q: What does the woman say about the fire department?
o: It gives a yearly safety lesson to students.
It is located next to the school.
It visits the school only in emergencies.
It teaches students to fight fires every week.
items.e: Visiting every year to teach safety means the department gives a yearly safety lesson.

L: You can get a free coffee refill if you keep your cup.
o: Save your cup and the next one is free.
Every customer gets a free cup to keep.
Refills cost extra if you keep your cup.
Coffee is free if you bring your own cup.
items.e: Keeping your cup lets you get a refill without paying.

L: The grocery store moved the bread to the back of the store.
o: At the back of the store
At the front of the store
Next to the checkout
Outside the store
items.e: It was moved to the back.

L: The volcano has been quiet for more than two hundred years.
items.q: What does the speaker say about the volcano?
o: It hasn't erupted for over two centuries.
It erupted last year
It is very active
It erupts every two years
items.e: "Quiet" means no eruption.

L: I'd like to deposit this check, but I left my debit card at home.
That's all right. As long as you have a photo ID, I can look up your account.
o: She can still make the deposit.
She has to come back with her card.
She needs a new photo for her ID.
He cannot find her account.
items.e: With a photo ID he can find her account, so the missing card is not a problem.

L: Did you get any good pictures at the lake?
Hardly any. I forgot to charge the camera battery, and it died after ten minutes.
o: She could take very few photos.
She lost her camera at the lake.
She took pictures for ten hours.
She had to buy a new battery.
items.e: "Hardly any" means almost none, because her camera stopped working after ten minutes.

L: My driver's license expires next week. Can I renew it online?
Not this time. You need a new photo, so you'll have to go in person.
items.q: What does the man tell the woman?
o: She must visit the office herself.
Her license has already expired.
She can do it online next week.
She needs to take a driving test.
items.e: Because she needs a new photo, she has to appear in person.

L: Can I get a large coffee with milk, no sugar?
Sure. Is that for here or to go?
To go, please. I'm already late for class.
items.q: What will the man probably do?
o: Take his drink with him
Drink his coffee at a table
Put some sugar in his coffee
Skip his class today
items.e: He orders the coffee to go because he is late for class.

L: Your Spanish has really improved. Have you been taking classes?
No, but I've been practicing with a coworker from Mexico during lunch every day.
items.q: How has the man improved his Spanish?
o: By talking with a colleague
By taking classes at lunch
By traveling to Mexico
By studying with a teacher
items.e: He practices every day with a coworker, not in a class.

L: How long is the wait for a table for four?
About forty-five minutes, but if you don't mind sitting at the counter, I can seat you right now.
o: A quicker option at the counter
A table for four right away
A free drink while they wait
A table outdoors in about five minutes
items.e: He can seat them immediately if they accept the counter instead of a table.

L: How often do your kids get to see their grandparents?
o: Only during summer vacation, sadly.
They're seventy and seventy-two.
My kids are both in fourth grade.
Their grandparents live in Maine.
items.e: "How often" asks about frequency, and the reply says only once a year in summer.

L: How far in advance do we need to book the inspection before moving out of quarters?
o: Housing likes about a month's notice.
We moved in last August, remember?
The inspector found a few problems.
It's not far, just past the gym.
items.e: A month's notice tells him how early to schedule the inspection.

L: Are you still going camping this weekend?
We were, but the forecast calls for storms, so we've put it off until next month.
o: She postponed her trip.
She canceled the trip for good.
She went camping in the storm.
She called off next month's trip.
items.e: "Put it off" means delay; the trip is now planned for next month.

L: Remember, we don't salute indoors except when formally reporting to an officer, so don't salute the captain in the hallway.
items.q: When should a soldier salute indoors?
o: When he officially reports to an officer.
Whenever he passes a captain in a hallway.
Each time any officer walks into the room.
Never, under any circumstances.
items.e: The only indoor salute mentioned is when a soldier formally reports to an officer.

L: The barracks fire drill went well, except that it took the third floor nearly twice as long to get out as everyone else.
items.q: What was the problem during the fire drill?
o: Some soldiers were much slower to leave.
The alarm didn't work on the third floor.
Everyone took twice as long as expected.
The drill had to be repeated twice.
items.e: Soldiers on the third floor needed almost twice as much time to leave the building as the others.

L: Promotions will be announced at the end of the month, but the ceremony itself won't take place until after the holidays.
items.q: When will the promotion ceremony be held?
o: After the holiday season.
At the end of this month.
Before the holidays begin.
On the day promotions are announced.
items.e: The names come out at the end of the month, but the ceremony is not until after the holidays.

L: Because the colonel is inspecting personally, the platoon sergeant wants our rooms ready by zero eight hundred, an hour earlier than planned.
items.q: By what time were the rooms first supposed to be ready?
o: Nine o'clock.
Eight o'clock.
Seven o'clock.
Ten o'clock.
items.e: The new time, 0800, is an hour earlier than planned, so the original time was 0900.

L: Stay on your post until the sergeant of the guard comes to relieve you, even if your shift is supposed to be over.
items.q: What does the man tell the guard to do?
o: Wait to be replaced before leaving.
Leave as soon as the shift ends.
Go and find the sergeant of the guard.
Relieve the sergeant at the end of the shift.
items.e: The guard may not leave the post until the sergeant of the guard relieves him.

L: Every soldier must finish the online equal opportunity course by the end of the quarter, or their promotions will be delayed.
items.q: What could happen to a soldier who skips the course?
o: His next promotion could come late.
He will have to retake it in a classroom.
He will lose his current rank.
He will finish at the end of the quarter.
items.e: Soldiers who do not finish the course on time will have their promotions delayed.

L: When you take over CQ, read the logbook from the last shift first, since it lists anything that still needs attention.
items.q: Why should the new CQ read the logbook?
o: To learn about unfinished business.
To sign out at the end of the shift.
To list the soldiers on the last shift.
To take attendance at formation.
items.e: The logbook shows what the previous shift left that still has to be done.

L: The mechanic said the brakes can wait another month, but the battery needs to be replaced before winter.
items.q: What does the car need first?
o: A new battery
New brakes
A winter tune-up
An oil change
items.e: The brakes can wait a month, but the battery has to be changed before winter.

L: This envelope needs extra postage because it's thicker than a quarter of an inch, even though it's light.
items.q: Why does the envelope cost more to mail?
o: Its size, not its weight, is the problem.
It weighs more than a quarter of a pound.
It is going to another country.
It needs to arrive by tomorrow.
items.e: The envelope is light but too thick, so the extra cost is because of its size.

L: Don't bother looking for the bus stop on Main Street; they moved it around the corner while the road is being repaved.
items.q: Why was the bus stop moved?
o: Work is being done on the road.
Buses no longer use Main Street at all.
Too many people were waiting there.
The corner is closer to the station.
items.e: The stop was moved because Main Street is being repaved.

L: We're third in line for takeoff, so it should be another ten minutes or so before we're in the air.
o: On a plane waiting to leave
In a line at the ticket counter
On a plane about to land
At the gate waiting to board
items.e: He is waiting in line for takeoff, so he is on a plane that has not left yet.

L: I'd planned to fly, but by the time I booked, the fares had doubled, so I'm driving the eight hours instead.
items.q: Why did the man change his plans?
o: Plane tickets became too expensive.
The flight was eight hours long.
He does not like flying.
All the flights were full.
items.e: The fares doubled before he booked, so he decided to drive.

L: Anyone caught speeding on post loses driving privileges for thirty days, no matter how many miles over the limit.
items.q: What happens to people who speed on post?
o: They cannot drive there for a month.
They pay a fine for each extra mile.
They lose their license for good.
They must drive thirty miles an hour.
items.e: Speeders lose the right to drive on post for thirty days.

L: The bridge has a weight limit of ten tons, so the fuel trucks will have to cross at the dam instead.
items.q: Why will the fuel trucks cross at the dam?
o: They are too heavy for the bridge.
The bridge is closed for repairs.
The dam is a shorter route.
They need to refuel at the dam.
items.e: The fuel trucks weigh more than the bridge's ten-ton limit.

L: Hurricane season doesn't officially end until November, so keep your emergency kit stocked even though it's been quiet lately.
o: Stay prepared for storms a while longer.
Restock the emergency kit in November.
Expect a hurricane before November.
Don't worry, because the season has already ended.
items.e: Hurricane season lasts until November, so people should keep their kits ready.

L: If a bee stings you, scrape the stinger out with a card instead of squeezing it with tweezers, which can push in more venom.
items.q: Why does the man advise against using tweezers?
o: They may make the sting worse.
They can break off the stinger.
They are hard to find in the field.
They can cause an infection.
items.e: Squeezing with tweezers can push more venom in, making the sting worse.

L: I've had this cough for nearly three weeks now, so I'm finally going to sick call tomorrow instead of waiting it out.
items.q: What has the man decided to do?
o: Get checked by medical staff.
Keep waiting for it to clear up.
Take three weeks off from work.
Buy medicine for his cough.
items.e: Going to sick call means he will be seen by medical staff.

L: Tornado sirens are tested at noon on the first Wednesday of each month, so if you hear them then, don't panic.
o: A siren at that time is only a test.
A tornado is expected on Wednesday.
Sirens should be reported at noon.
People should take cover every Wednesday.
items.e: The sirens are tested at that time, so hearing them then is not an emergency.

L: Frostbitten fingers should be warmed slowly in warm, not hot, water, and you should never rub them to get the blood flowing.
items.q: Which action does the man warn against?
o: Rubbing the affected fingers.
Soaking the fingers in warm water.
Warming the hands gradually.
Keeping the fingers covered.
items.e: He says never to rub frostbitten fingers.

L: I was going to give blood today, but they turned me away because I'd just gotten back from a country with malaria.
items.q: Why couldn't the man donate blood?
o: His recent trip disqualified him.
He had come down with malaria.
He was too tired from his trip.
The blood drive was canceled today.
items.e: He was turned away because he had recently been in a country with malaria.

L: The wind is gusting to forty miles an hour, so the parachute jump has been scrubbed, and they'll try again at first light tomorrow.
items.q: What happened to the parachute jump?
o: It was postponed until tomorrow.
It was moved to later this evening.
It took place in strong winds.
It was finished at first light.
items.e: "Scrubbed" means canceled; they will try again tomorrow at dawn.

L: Our instructor won't let us use our phones in class, not even to look up a word in a translation app.
items.q: What does the man say about his class?
o: Phones are completely banned during lessons.
Students may use phones to translate words.
The instructor uses a translation app in class.
Students must turn in their phones before class.
items.e: Phones may not be used in class for any reason, even for translating a word.

L: I'd rather finish this report tonight than come in early tomorrow, because the inspection team arrives at eight sharp.
items.q: What does the man prefer to do?
o: Stay late to complete his work
Arrive early tomorrow morning
Ask the inspectors to come later
Finish the report after the inspection
items.e: "I'd rather finish this report tonight" means he prefers to work late instead of coming in early.

L: I've filled out this leave form three times already, and personnel keeps sending it back because of small mistakes.
items.q: How does the man probably feel?
o: Annoyed
Relieved
Grateful
Bored
items.e: Having the same form returned again and again is irritating.

L: Solar panels still produce some electricity on cloudy days, but far less than they do in bright sunshine.
items.q: What does the man say about solar panels?
o: Their output drops when the sky is overcast.
They stop working completely on cloudy days.
They produce more power when it's cloudy.
They work only in very hot weather.
items.e: On cloudy days the panels make much less electricity, but they do not stop completely.

L: You can't bring cell phones into this building, so leave yours in the locker at the entrance.
items.q: What does the man tell the listener to do?
o: Store the phone before going inside.
Turn off the phone inside the building.
Bring the phone to the entrance.
Lock the building when leaving.
items.e: Phones are not allowed inside, so the listener must put the phone in a locker first.

L: Please keep personal calls short during duty hours, because the phone in this office is for official business.
o: Limit private conversations at work.
Make personal calls after duty hours only.
Use the office phone for personal business.
Never answer the phone during duty hours.
items.e: He asks people to keep personal calls brief while on duty.

L: I thought the application for the leadership course was due next Friday, but it turns out it closed yesterday.
o: It is too late to apply.
He has a week left to apply.
The course was canceled yesterday.
The course begins next Friday.
items.e: The application period ended yesterday, so he has missed the deadline.

L: The steak was a little overcooked, but the service was so friendly that I left a bigger tip than usual.
items.q: How did the man feel about the restaurant?
o: He liked the staff more than the food.
He thought the steak was cooked perfectly.
He was unhappy and left no tip.
He thought the service was too slow.
items.e: The steak was overcooked, but the friendly service earned a larger tip, so he was more pleased with the staff than the meal.

L: I'd rather not carry cash when I travel, so I usually let my bank know where I'm going and use my card.
items.q: What does the man usually do before a trip?
o: Notify his bank of his destination.
Take out a lot of cash from his bank.
Order a replacement card from his bank.
Ask his bank for a small travel loan.
items.e: He tells his bank where he is going so he can use his card instead of cash.

L: The used car looks great, but I won't buy it until my mechanic has had a chance to look under the hood.
items.q: What will the man do before deciding?
o: Have the car inspected.
Buy it right away.
Ask for a lower price.
Test-drive a different car.
items.e: He wants his mechanic to check the engine before he makes a decision.

L: The credit union pays almost twice the interest my bank does on savings, so I'm moving my money over there.
items.q: Why is the man switching to the credit union?
o: He can earn more on his deposits.
It charges less interest on loans.
His bank is twice as far away.
He needs to borrow money from it.
items.e: The credit union pays nearly double the interest, so his savings will grow faster there.

L: My oldest friend is moving overseas next month, so a few of us are throwing him a going-away party on Friday.
items.q: What is the purpose of Friday's party?
o: To say goodbye to someone who is leaving.
To welcome a friend back from overseas.
To celebrate the man's new job abroad.
To help a friend pack for his move.
items.e: A going-away party is held for someone who is leaving; his friend is moving abroad.

L: That new Italian place doesn't take reservations, so if we want a table on Friday night, we'd better get there before six.
o: Showing up early to get a seat.
Calling ahead to reserve a table.
Trying a different restaurant.
Eating there after six on Friday.
items.e: Because the restaurant does not take reservations, they should arrive before six to get a table.

L: The kennel charges thirty-five dollars a night, so it's cheaper to pay my nephew to stay with our dog.
items.q: What will the man probably do with his dog?
o: Have a relative look after it.
Board it at the kennel nearby.
Bring it along on the trip.
Have a neighbor feed it daily.
items.e: The kennel is expensive, so he will pay his nephew, a family member, to care for the dog.

L: Our team was behind by six points at halftime, but we outscored them by ten in the second half.
items.q: What was the result of the game?
o: The man's team won by four points.
The man's team lost by four points.
The man's team won by ten points.
The game ended in a tie.
items.e: Six points down, then ten points better in the second half, means a four-point win.

L: The scoreboard says we lost, three to two, but the referee didn't count our last goal because time had already run out.
items.q: What does the man say about his team's last goal?
o: It came after the game had ended.
It tied the game at three.
The referee allowed it wrongly.
It was scored by the other team.
items.e: The goal did not count because it was scored after time had run out.

L: The commissary is closed on Mondays; otherwise it's open nine to seven, except Sundays, when it closes at five.
items.q: On which day could someone shop there at six in the evening?
o: On a Saturday.
On a Monday.
On a Sunday.
Only on weekends.
items.e: Saturday hours run until seven, but on Sunday it closes at five and on Monday it is closed.

L: I need to be at the airfield by fifteen hundred, and it's a forty-minute drive, so I'll leave no later than fourteen fifteen.
items.q: How much extra time is the man allowing himself?
o: About five minutes.
About fifteen minutes.
About forty minutes.
About forty-five minutes.
items.e: Leaving at fourteen fifteen and driving forty minutes puts him there at fourteen fifty-five, five minutes early.

L: Ten of us signed up for the ski trip, but the van only holds eight, so two people will have to drive themselves.
items.q: What does the man say about the trip?
o: Not everyone fits in the van.
Two vans will be needed.
Only eight people signed up.
All ten will ride in the van.
items.e: Ten people signed up and the van holds eight, so two cannot ride in it.

L: Our convoy averaged fifty kilometers an hour on the highway, but only half that speed once we hit the mountain roads.
items.q: How fast did the convoy go in the mountains?
o: About twenty-five kilometers an hour.
About fifty kilometers an hour.
About one hundred kilometers an hour.
About forty kilometers an hour.
items.e: Half of fifty kilometers an hour is twenty-five.

L: I had hoped to get the tires for under four hundred dollars, but the cheapest set was four fifty, plus fifty for installation.
items.q: What was the total cost of the cheapest option?
o: Five hundred dollars.
Four hundred fifty dollars.
Four hundred dollars.
Five hundred fifty dollars.
items.e: Four hundred fifty for the tires plus fifty for installation comes to five hundred dollars.

L: How come you didn't qualify? You were hitting everything during practice yesterday.
o: I guess my nerves got the better of me.
Thanks, I'll see you at practice tomorrow, then.
I hit the gym every day after work.
No, I didn't go to the range yesterday.
items.e: She gives the reason she failed: she was too nervous when it really counted.

L: How long has your shoulder kept you out of PT?
o: Ever since I fell on the obstacle course.
My shoulder is a little higher.
About two inches longer than the other one.
I'll keep it out of the rain.
items.e: She dates the problem from the time she was hurt on the obstacle course.

L: How did your room do on the fire safety inspection last night?
o: They took away our coffee maker.
The fire station is down the road.
I did it the night before.
My room is on the third floor.
items.e: She implies the room did not pass completely: an item that was not allowed was removed.

L: Isn't it about time we changed the batteries in these handsets?
o: I swapped them out just before lunch.
It's about ten after three.
I changed my mind about the trip.
These hand warmers work great.
items.e: She means it isn't necessary because she put new batteries in only a short time ago.

L: How come there are two guards at the back gate tonight instead of one?
o: Security's tighter while the general's here.
One of them came back an hour ago.
The back gate is next to the gym.
I'd rather go by myself tonight.
items.e: She explains that extra guards were added because of an important visitor.

L: How are you going to stay in touch with your family while you're overseas?
o: Video calls, whenever the internet works.
My family lives overseas, too.
I'm staying at a hotel in town.
We touched down late in the evening.
items.e: She explains how she will communicate with her family.

L: If I take leave next week, who's going to cover my shift in the motor pool?
o: Relax. Jenkins already offered.
The motor pool is closed on weekends.
I'll take the next one, thanks.
Put a cover on it, or it'll get wet.
items.e: She tells him a coworker has volunteered to do his shift.

L: This package has to reach Germany by Friday. What's the fastest way to send it?
o: Express mail, but it isn't cheap.
It reached Germany last Friday.
I'll be there just as fast as I can.
Just pack it in a bigger box.
items.e: She names the quickest service and warns him that it costs a lot.

L: Isn't it a little early to start packing? Your move isn't until next month.
o: Not with three kids and a garage full of stuff.
Yes, I moved in here last month.
I packed a lunch for you this morning.
The class starts early next month.
items.e: She means it is not too early because her family has so many things to pack.

L: I thought you swapped shifts with Sergeant Long. How come you're here so early?
o: He changed his mind at the last minute.
I've been here a long time, actually.
Please turn the switch off before you leave.
He's been a sergeant for a long time.
items.e: She explains that the swap did not happen because the sergeant changed his plans.

L: Who's supposed to send out the minutes from yesterday's meeting? I haven't seen them.
o: That's usually Lieutenant Park's job.
It lasted about forty-five minutes.
I haven't seen him since yesterday.
I'm supposed to be out of here by noon.
items.e: She names the person who normally sends them.

L: Is the safety briefing this afternoon mandatory, or can I skip it if I'm busy?
o: They take attendance, so I'd go.
The kids are skipping rope outside.
The brief was very short.
Sorry, I've been busy all week.
items.e: She implies it is required because attendance is checked.

L: I just got an e-mail asking for my password. That's not from our IT people, is it?
o: No way. Report it right away.
I passed it on to the people upstairs.
Yes, I just sent you an e-mail.
My password is the same as yours.
items.e: She tells him the message is a fake and he should report it.

L: The forecast says snow in the pass tonight. Shouldn't we wait until morning to drive?
o: Agreed. Let's leave at first light.
I passed my driving test on the first try.
It snowed a lot yesterday morning.
I'll wait for you out in the car.
items.e: She agrees to delay the trip and set off as soon as it gets light.

L: How come the train hasn't left yet? It was supposed to depart at nine.
o: Something's wrong with one of the doors.
It's on the left side, next to platform nine.
I suppose I'll come along, then.
I usually leave home around nine.
items.e: She explains the delay: a door is not working.

L: Let me help you with that suitcase. It looks heavier than you are.
o: Thanks. I may have packed too much.
It looks like it might rain later.
I'm heavier than I used to be.
The suit was too big for me.
items.e: She accepts his help and admits her suitcase is too full.

L: Would it be possible to get a room on a lower floor?
o: Let me see what we have available.
The price is lower on weekends.
The floor is still wet from the mop.
It's possible that he's in his room.
items.e: She offers to check whether such a room is free.

L: Could you tell me whether this train stops at the airport?
o: No, you'll have to change at Central.
It stopped raining an hour ago.
The weather at the airport is fine.
I'll tell him to stop by later.
items.e: She tells him this train does not go to the airport, so he must switch trains.

L: I've never traveled abroad before. What's the first thing I should do?
o: Apply for your passport right away.
I traveled there first last year.
It's a broad street downtown.
I've been there twice before.
items.e: She advises him to start by getting a passport.

L: Would you rather sit by the window or on the aisle for this flight?
o: I like being able to get up easily.
I'd rather not open the window.
The flight was smooth, wasn't it?
I'll sit with you at lunch.
items.e: She prefers the aisle seat because she can leave it without bothering anyone.

L: Do you think it's too late to send out invitations for Saturday's birthday party?
o: Maybe. Why not just call everyone?
I was only about ten minutes late.
She'll be turning seven on Saturday.
I sent mine to the wrong address.
items.e: She suggests phoning the guests, which is faster than mailing invitations.

L: Why don't we paint the living room ourselves instead of hiring someone?
o: Fine, as long as you do the ceiling.
They're hiring at the hardware store.
Because the paint was still wet.
My room is at the end of the hall.
items.e: She accepts the suggestion on one condition.

L: That jacket looks great on you. Why don't you go ahead and buy it?
o: I'd like to, but it's too expensive.
Because I bought it a week ahead.
It looks like rain later this afternoon.
Go ahead, I'll catch up with you.
items.e: She would like to buy it but cannot afford it.

L: Are you going to finish your fries, or can I have a couple?
o: Go ahead. I couldn't eat another bite.
I finished the whole book on Friday.
We've been a couple for about two years.
I'd like mine with extra salt.
items.e: She offers him the fries because she is full.

L: I can't find the remote anywhere. Did one of the kids take it to their room?
o: Did you look under the cushions?
Their rooms are both upstairs.
The kids took the bus to school.
It's a very remote area up there.
items.e: She suggests a more likely place to look for it.

L: My mother-in-law is staying with us for a month. Can you believe it?
o: Wow. Do you two get along?
I believe the meeting is on Monday.
She stayed at a hotel last month.
My mother is a lawyer, too.
items.e: She reacts to the news and asks a natural follow-up question.

L: Do you happen to know if we can leave early once we finish the listening part?
o: Only after they've collected the papers.
I left my headphones out in the car again.
The listening part was the easiest for me.
We usually finish early on Fridays.
items.e: She says leaving is allowed, but only once the test papers have been collected.

L: How come you're taking the evening class instead of the one in the morning?
o: My shift doesn't end until noon.
It starts at seven in the evening.
I'll take the early bus instead.
Come by in the morning, if you can.
items.e: She explains that her work schedule keeps her busy in the morning.

L: The pharmacy said my prescription won't be ready until tomorrow. Can I get it filled anywhere else?
o: The drugstore by the gate might have it.
I'll be ready to leave whenever you are.
Fill it up with regular gas, please.
She told me it would come tomorrow.
items.e: She suggests another place where he could get his medicine sooner.

L: I'm thinking about dropping the math course. It's taking up all my free time.
o: Why not talk to the instructor first?
Of course, it's free for everyone.
I dropped by your office this morning.
I took it up as a hobby last year.
items.e: She suggests he speak with the teacher before deciding to quit the course.

L: Do you know where I can find a quiet place to study? The barracks are too noisy.
o: The library stays open until ten.
Yes, I found it under the bed last night.
It's been pretty quiet around here lately.
I studied there for about two years.
items.e: She suggests the library as a quiet place where he can study in the evening.

L: Don't you think the teacher went over the new grammar a little too fast today?
o: Totally. I was completely lost.
I went over to his house today.
My grandma is visiting this week.
Don't worry, I'll drive slower.
items.e: She agrees, saying she could not follow the lesson.

L: The medic said I should take these pills with food. Does that mean before or after eating?
o: During the meal is best.
I took them before I left.
The food here is pretty good.
He said it after lunch.
items.e: She explains that the pills should be taken while eating.

L: Can I just skip the online part of the course? I'll be at the schoolhouse in person in March anyway.
Afraid not. They won't even let you sign in at the front desk without the certificate showing you finished it.
o: Completing the online portion is required first.
The front desk will issue his certificate in March.
He can do the online part at the schoolhouse.
The course in March has been canceled.
items.e: Without proof that he finished the online part, he cannot report for the course.

L: A civilian at the barracks door says he's here to visit his brother. It's almost midnight.
Visiting hours ended at ten. Take his name and phone number, and tell him to come back tomorrow.
items.q: What does the woman tell the man to do?
o: Send the visitor away for tonight
Let the visitor stay in until ten
Call the brother's phone number
Go upstairs and wake up the brother
items.e: Visiting hours are over, so the man should turn the visitor away until tomorrow.

L: The serial number on this rifle doesn't match the one on my hand receipt.
Don't sign anything yet. Let me pull the property book; someone may have swapped weapons during the last turn-in.
o: Two rifles were mixed up earlier.
The man has signed the wrong form.
The property book has been lost.
Someone stole the man's rifle.
items.e: She thinks weapons may have been exchanged by mistake at the last turn-in.

L: I made the list for staff sergeant, but my enlistment ends in eight months.
Then you'll have to extend or reenlist before they'll pin it on. Have you talked to the career counselor?
items.q: What does the woman say about the promotion?
o: He must commit to more service to get it.
It will be canceled in eight months.
The career counselor must approve it first.
He can receive it after he leaves the Army.
items.e: He cannot be promoted unless he stays in longer by extending or reenlisting.

L: How did your practice class go at the instructor course?
My material was fine, but I ran twelve minutes over. The evaluator said if it happens again, I'll be dropped.
items.q: What was the problem with the woman's class?
o: She went past the time limit.
Her lesson content was weak.
She arrived twelve minutes late.
The evaluator left early.
items.e: She ran over the allowed time by twelve minutes.

L: I passed the written test for the five-ton. When can I start driving it on missions?
Not until you log ten hours behind the wheel with an instructor. Then there's the road test.
items.q: What can be concluded about the man?
o: He still has more steps to complete.
He failed the road test last week.
He can drive on missions next week.
He needs ten hours of classroom study.
items.e: He must finish supervised driving hours and a road test before driving on missions.

L: I turned in my leave form two weeks ago, and I still haven't heard anything.
That's odd. The commander signed a whole stack yesterday. Check with the orderly room before you buy any tickets.
items.q: What does the woman advise the man to do?
o: Find out whether his request went through
Buy his tickets as soon as possible
Turn in another copy of the form
Ask the commander for a signature
items.e: She tells him to check with the orderly room to find out whether his request was signed before buying tickets.

L: I've been transferred three times, and every office tells me to call someone else.
I'm sorry about that, sir. Give me your number, and I'll have the right person get back to you within the hour.
items.q: What will the woman probably do?
o: Arrange a callback for him
Transfer him to another office
Call him back three times
Give him her own number
items.e: She takes his number so the right person can call him back within an hour.

L: I got my new laptop this morning, but I can't do anything with it.
That's because your account hasn't been created yet. It usually takes IT two or three days after you sign the user agreement.
items.q: Why can't the man use his laptop?
o: His network access is not ready yet.
He has not received the laptop yet.
IT is repairing it for two days.
He lost his user agreement.
items.e: His user account has not been set up yet.

L: According to my pay statement, I only have six days of leave left. I thought I had sixteen.
Did you count the ten days you took over Christmas? They might not have been charged until this month.
o: His time off in December may be the reason.
His statement has a typing error.
He should take six days before Christmas.
He earned ten extra days this month.
items.e: The ten days he took at Christmas may have just been subtracted, which explains the lower balance.

L: The fifteenth is a Sunday this month. Does that mean we don't get paid until Monday?
Just the opposite. When payday lands on a weekend, the money comes on the Friday before.
o: On the thirteenth
On the fifteenth
On the sixteenth
On the seventeenth
items.e: The fifteenth is a Sunday, so the Friday before it is the thirteenth.

L: The printer says the black cartridge is empty, but I just replaced it on Monday.
Did you pull off the plastic tape? It won't print at all if that's still on.
items.q: What does the woman think is wrong?
o: Something was left on the new cartridge.
The cartridge was put in upside down.
The printer needs a new cartridge.
The cartridge was replaced too early.
items.e: She thinks he left the plastic tape on the new cartridge.

L: Do I have to set up the electric bill myself when I move into post housing?
No, utilities are included. But if you go over the monthly baseline, you'll get a bill for the extra.
o: Heavy use could cost him money.
He must open an electric account.
Utilities cost extra every month.
Post housing has no monthly limit.
items.e: Utilities are free up to a monthly limit, but he pays for anything above it.

L: Excuse me, will this bag fit in the overhead bin?
It's a bit over the size limit, sir. We'll tag it here, and it'll be waiting for you on the jet bridge when you land.
items.q: What will happen to the man's bag?
o: He'll collect it as he gets off.
It will go in the overhead bin.
It will be sent to baggage claim.
It will stay behind at the gate.
items.e: The bag is too big for the cabin, so it will be checked at the gate and returned to him on the jet bridge.

L: I only need a one-way ticket to Philadelphia, but it costs more than a round trip.
That happens all the time. Buy the round trip and just don't use the return half.
o: Choosing the cheaper fare anyway
Waiting for the price to come down
Coming back from Philadelphia by bus
Asking for a refund on the return trip
items.e: The round trip is cheaper, so she says to buy it and simply skip the trip back.

L: Should I take the toll road to the airport? I don't have any cash on me.
The rental has a transponder on the windshield, so the tolls just go on your bill.
o: He won't need money at the booths.
He should avoid the road with tolls.
He must stop and pay with a card.
The windshield on the rental is cracked.
items.e: A device in the car records the tolls and adds them to his bill, so he needs no cash.

L: Weren't we supposed to turn at that last light?
Oh no, you're right. I was so busy talking I didn't even notice. Let's turn around at the next driveway.
o: She drove past their turn.
The traffic light was not working.
The man was talking on the phone.
They took the wrong driveway.
items.e: She was talking and missed the light where they should have turned.

L: The only hotel near the course charges a hundred and forty a night, and my lodging allowance is only one twenty.
Then either you cover the difference yourself, or you look a little farther out.
items.q: How much more than the man's allowance does the hotel cost per night?
o: Twenty dollars
Forty dollars
Fourteen dollars
Twelve dollars
items.e: The hotel costs one hundred forty dollars and his allowance is one hundred twenty, a difference of twenty.

L: Has anyone from the new unit contacted you about your arrival?
Yes, my sponsor emailed. She's meeting me at the airport and has already reserved a room for me.
items.q: What has the woman's sponsor already done?
o: Arranged a place for her to stay
Emailed the new unit about her
Met her at the airport yesterday
Booked her a plane ticket to the base
items.e: The sponsor has reserved a room and will meet her at the airport later.

L: Have they ordered an evacuation for the base yet?
Not yet, but they're saying it could come by noon. I'd load the car now so we don't get stuck in traffic.
o: Packing up ahead of time
Staying on base until noon
Driving through heavy traffic
Unloading the car after the storm
items.e: She wants to be ready to leave before the order comes and the roads fill up.

L: I'm heading out for a run. It's already getting dark, though.
Then grab your reflective belt. Drivers on Perimeter Road can hardly see runners after sunset.
items.q: Why does the woman tell the man to take the belt?
o: So that he is visible to traffic
So that he can run on Perimeter Road
Because it is required at the gym
Because drivers must stop for runners
items.e: She says drivers can hardly see runners after dark, so the belt helps them notice him.

L: Did the clinic call you back about your blood test?
They did. Everything came back normal, but they want me to cut down on salt and come back in six months.
items.q: What can be concluded about the woman?
o: She does not have a serious problem.
She must return to the clinic next month.
She needs another blood test today.
She has stopped eating salt completely.
items.e: Her results were normal; she only needs to eat less salt and have a routine follow-up.

L: This floor cleaner isn't working very well. Want me to mix in some bleach?
Absolutely not. Those two together can give off toxic fumes. Just scrub harder.
o: Mixing them could harm their health.
Bleach would damage the floor.
The cleaner works well enough already.
They have run out of bleach.
items.e: Combining bleach with other cleaners can produce poisonous gases.

L: My tooth has been killing me since last night, but the dental clinic's next opening is three weeks out.
With pain like that, go to dental sick call in the morning. They'll see you the same day.
o: Urgent cases are seen without a wait.
He has to wait three weeks for care.
The clinic is open only in the morning.
He should take something for the pain.
items.e: Patients in serious pain can go to sick call and be treated that same day.

L: I'd like a workout plan, but personal trainers downtown charge a fortune.
Have you asked at the fitness center on post? They have trainers on staff, and the sessions don't cost a thing.
items.q: What does the woman tell the man?
o: Training help is available at no charge.
Trainers downtown are worth the money.
The post gym is closed to new members.
He should design his own workout plan.
items.e: "Don't cost a thing" means the trainers at the post fitness center are free.

L: The bill came to a hundred and forty dollars. How much should we leave for the tip?
Look at the bottom. They've already added eighteen percent because we're a big group, so we're all set.
o: They don't need to add anything more.
They should leave eighteen percent.
The bill is wrong at the bottom.
The group should split the bill.
items.e: The tip is already included in the bill, so "we're all set" means nothing more is needed.

L: Why did the MP stop you this morning? You were only jogging.
I had my earbuds in. Apparently they're not allowed while running on post roads because you can't hear traffic coming.
o: She was wearing something not allowed.
She was jogging on the wrong side.
She did not hear the MP calling.
She was running too close to traffic.
items.e: Earbuds are not permitted while running on post roads.

L: Honey, did you remember to sign Emma's permission slip for the field trip?
Oh no, it's still on the refrigerator. Can you drop it off at the school on your way to work?
items.q: What does the woman ask the man to do?
o: Take a form to the school
Sign the slip for her
Drive Emma on the field trip
Put the slip on the refrigerator
items.e: She asks him to deliver the permission slip to the school as he goes to work.

L: My mother-in-law is staying with us for a month. Any advice?
Give her something to do. When my mom visited, she reorganized my whole kitchen, and honestly, I didn't mind one bit.
o: Keeping a guest busy can be helpful.
Her mother made her kitchen messy.
A month is too long for a visit.
She was upset with her mother.
items.e: Her mother's project in the kitchen worked out well, so giving a visitor a task is a good idea.

L: Did the kids finish their homework before they went outside to play?
They told me they did, but I found Sarah's math worksheet under the couch, completely blank.
o: At least one child did not tell the truth.
Sarah finished her math before playing.
The children are doing homework outside.
The worksheet was lost under the bed.
items.e: The kids said they were done, but Sarah's worksheet had nothing on it.

L: Where's the remote? I've looked everywhere in the living room.
Did you check the baby's toy box? Last time we found your car keys in there.
o: The baby may have taken the remote.
The car keys are in the living room.
The man left the remote out in the car.
The toy box is in the living room.
items.e: The baby hid the keys before, so the baby may have put the remote in the toy box too.

L: Did you tell your dad we're selling the old family car?
Not yet. He taught me to drive in that car, so I'm waiting for the right moment.
items.q: Why hasn't the woman told her father?
o: The car has sentimental value.
He wants to buy the car himself.
He doesn't know how to drive.
She hasn't decided to sell yet.
items.e: The car holds special memories, so she wants to break the news carefully.

L: Mom called. She's wondering if we can host the family reunion this summer.
In this little house? We'd have people sleeping in the bathtub. Maybe we could rent a cabin instead.
o: Their home doesn't have enough room.
Renting a cabin costs too much money.
Summer is a busy time for the family.
She doesn't get along with his mother.
items.e: Their house is too small for all the relatives.

L: There's a strange smell in the hallway, kind of like rotten eggs.
That could be a gas leak. Get everyone outside and call the gas company from the yard, not from in here.
items.q: What does the woman tell the man to do first?
o: Leave the house
Open the windows
Look for the leak
Clean the hallway
items.e: She wants everyone out of the house before anyone makes a call.

L: I understand almost everything the instructor says, but when I have to speak, my mind goes blank.
Try chatting with the American students at the gym. Practice makes it a lot easier.
o: He has trouble expressing himself aloud.
He cannot follow the instructor's lessons.
He has no time to go to the gym.
He forgets what he reads in class.
items.e: He understands well, but he cannot think of what to say when he must talk.

L: Your bread smells great. When did you start baking?
Last winter, when I was snowed in for a week with nothing to do. Now I can't stop.
items.q: Why did the woman start baking?
o: She was stuck at home and bored.
She wanted to sell bread to friends.
She took a class last winter.
Her family gave her a new oven.
items.e: Snow kept her inside for a week with nothing to do, so she tried baking.

L: I studied the wrong chapter for today's quiz. I thought we were still on chapter six.
No wonder you looked confused. We finished six last week.
o: He reviewed something already covered.
He skipped chapter six completely.
He missed the quiz last week.
He studied a chapter they haven't reached.
items.e: The class finished chapter six last week, so he studied old material.

L: I missed three days of class with the flu. I'm afraid I've fallen way behind.
Don't panic. I'll lend you my notes, and we can go over the hard parts on Saturday.
o: To help him catch up on the lessons
To teach the class on Saturday
To call the instructor for him
To take him to the doctor
items.e: She will give him her notes and review the difficult material with him.

L: Math was never my strong point, and now I need it for the electronics course.
The education center offers free tutoring on weekday evenings. Lots of people in my unit go.
o: He can get extra help at no cost.
He should drop the electronics course.
Her unit teaches math on weekends.
Tutoring would be too expensive for him.
items.e: She tells him about free evening tutoring that could help him with math.

L: I tried to register for the evening English class, but it's already full.
Put your name on the waiting list. Someone always drops out during the first week.
items.q: What does the woman think will happen?
o: A space will probably open up soon.
The class will be canceled next week.
He'll have to take a morning class.
She'll drop the class for him.
items.e: Students usually quit early, so a seat is likely to become free.

L: My neighbor's band practices in his garage every evening until ten. I can't even hear my own TV.
Have you talked to him? He might not realize how far the sound carries.
o: Mentioning the noise to the neighbor
Turning up his television even louder
Joining the neighbor's band
Calling the military police at ten
items.e: She thinks the neighbor may not know he is too loud, so the man should tell him.

L: Excuse me, could you tell me whether this treadmill is reserved, or can I use it?
o: Go ahead. Nobody's signed up for it this hour.
I reserved a table for six at seven o'clock tonight.
I usually use it to warm up before lifting.
Sorry, I can't tell you the time right now.
items.e: He tells her the machine is free because no one has booked it.

L: The sergeant asked me to lead the next class on first aid. Any advice?
o: Keep the lecture short and give them lots of practice.
There's a first aid kit in my truck, I think.
She asked me the same thing on Tuesday afternoon.
Follow me. I'll lead you to the classroom.
items.e: He gives teaching advice: talk less and let the students practice.

L: During my walk-through, I noticed the fire extinguisher tags on the second floor are all from last year.
Then they're past due for inspection. Put in a work order with the fire department before the inspectors catch it.
o: The extinguishers are overdue for a check.
A fire started on the second floor.
The inspectors found missing extinguishers.
The fire department lost the work order.
items.e: The tags show the last inspection was a year ago, so a new one is overdue.

L: The inspector gave my room a failing grade, and I spent all night cleaning.
Did you remember the top of your wall locker? That's the first place Sergeant Diaz runs his finger.
items.q: What does the woman think the man probably forgot?
o: To dust a high surface
To make his bed properly
To clean the floor under his bed
To lock his wall locker
items.e: She suggests he missed the dust on top of his locker, which the sergeant always checks.

L: Do we really have to show up for the graduation rehearsal at seven? I know where to stand.
The commandant made it mandatory. Last year two students who skipped it weren't allowed to march at all.
o: He could be left out of the ceremony.
The rehearsal begins later than seven.
Two students failed the course last year.
The commandant will not attend this year.
items.e: Students who missed the rehearsal last year could not take part in the ceremony.

L: It's pouring. Are we still practicing with the colors on the parade field this afternoon?
We'll move into the gym. The flags can't get soaked, but the ceremony's Monday, so we can't skip practice either.
o: Practice will be held indoors.
Practice will be canceled because of rain.
The ceremony will be moved to Monday.
The team will practice without the flags.
items.e: To protect the flags and still prepare for Monday, they will practice in the gym.

L: Have you finished the project management course your supervisor recommended?
I finished every module yesterday, but the certificate still won't print. I've emailed the help desk twice.
o: She has no proof of completion yet.
She failed the final module yesterday.
Her supervisor did not recommend it.
The help desk is closed this week.
items.e: She completed the course, but she can't print the certificate.

L: The sign on the bridge says twenty tons. Our loaded truck is close to twenty-five.
Then we're not crossing here. Get on the radio and find out if the north route is open.
o: Take a different way
Unload the truck first
Cross the bridge slowly
Wait for the sign to change
items.e: The truck is too heavy for the bridge, so they will look for another route.

L: The kids want to go to the zoo tomorrow, but it's supposed to be ninety-eight degrees.
Then let's get there when it opens at nine. Most of the animals hide in the shade by noon anyway.
o: Going early to avoid the heat
Waiting for cooler weather next week
Visiting the zoo at noon
Staying in the shade all day
items.e: She wants to arrive at opening time, before the hottest part of the day.

L: How long do we have to load the trucks before the convoy leaves, Sergeant?
o: About forty-five minutes.
About forty-five miles an hour.
About forty-five crates.
About forty-five dollars.
items.e: How long asks about time, so the answer is a length of time.

L: The change-of-command ceremony was already under way when the general's car finally pulled up to the parade ground.
items.q: What was happening when the general arrived?
o: It was already in progress
It was just about to begin
It had been called off
It was moved to another day
items.e: Under way means that something has already started.

L: Senior Airman Khan never goes to the movies by himself; he always waits until someone can come along.
items.q: What does Senior Airman Khan prefer?
o: Going with a friend
Watching films at home
Going to the late show
Buying tickets in advance
items.e: He never goes alone and waits for company, so he likes going with someone.

L: Nobody in the entire squadron was late for the opening ceremony, and the colonel noticed it right away.
items.q: What does the speaker say about the squadron?
o: Every member arrived on time
A few members came late
The colonel was the last to arrive
Half of them stayed away
items.e: Nobody in the entire squadron was late means every member was on time.

L: Marlow Falls turned into a manufacturing town decades ago, and almost everyone on my street worked on a production line.
items.q: How did most of the speaker's neighbors earn a living?
o: They built products in plants
They grew crops on farms
They served guests at hotels
They taught at the local school
items.e: A manufacturing town is one where people make goods in plants and factories.

L: Minor crashes happen most often in heavy traffic, when drivers are tired and in a hurry to get home.
items.q: When are minor crashes most common?
o: When the roads are crowded
When the weather is very hot
When the streets are empty
When the cars are brand new
items.e: Heavy traffic means crowded roads, where small accidents happen most.

L: The ground crew found a dent near the tail of the helicopter after the storm, so it can't fly until Friday.
items.q: What part of the helicopter was dented?
o: The back end
The front window
The left door
The top blades
items.e: The tail is at the rear of an aircraft.

L: Corporal Ahmed gave the lieutenant a good reason for missing formation: a flat tire had held him up on the highway.
items.q: What did Corporal Ahmed tell the lieutenant?
o: Why he was not at formation
When formation would be held
How he planned to fix the tire
Where he would go next
items.e: A reason for missing formation explains why he was not there.

L: It's a long drive. Are you comfortable back there, or should I move my seat up?
o: I'm fine. I've got plenty of legroom.
Yes, I moved up here last spring.
It takes about six hours, depending on traffic.
No, I'd rather not drive tonight.
items.e: He says he is fine and has enough space, so he is comfortable.
