L: Specialist Moore reached the bus station at half past six, but his bus didn't leave until eight.
items.q: How long did Specialist Moore wait for the bus?
o: Ninety minutes
Two and a half hours
Thirty minutes
Two hours
items.e: From six thirty until eight is an hour and a half, or ninety minutes.

L: That was a great dinner. Do you want dessert, or shall we ask for the check?
o: Let's share a piece of apple pie.
No, I paid by credit card.
I'd like my steak well done.
Yes, we ate dinner at seven.
items.e: Dessert is the sweet course at the end of a meal, and sharing a pie answers the question.

L: The drops the eye doctor gave Petty Officer Lund left his vision blurred for two hours, so his wife drove him home.
items.q: Why did Petty Officer Lund's wife drive him home?
o: He couldn't see properly.
His car was in the shop.
He felt sick to his stomach.
His glasses were broken.
items.e: Blurred vision means things look unclear, so he could not see well enough to drive.

L: Corporal Fenwick plans to spend about forty dollars on a new pair of running shoes at the PX this weekend.
items.q: What is Corporal Fenwick going to do?
o: Buy some athletic footwear
Repair his old running shoes
Sell his shoes for forty dollars
Run forty miles this weekend
items.e: To spend forty dollars on shoes means to buy them.

L: The roads are icy tonight, so my wife made me promise to drive slowly and take no chances on the way home.
items.q: What does the man's wife want him to be?
o: Careful while driving
Home before dark
Brave on the icy roads
Quick on the highway
items.e: Driving slowly and taking no chances means being careful.

L: Before the morning march, the supply clerk distributed warm gloves to every soldier in the platoon.
items.q: What did the supply clerk do?
o: He gave a pair to everyone.
He took the gloves back at night.
He gave all the gloves to one soldier.
He sold the gloves to the soldiers.
items.e: To distribute means to give out items to everyone in a group.

L: The label on this new antenna says terrestrial use only, so the crew will bolt it to the roof of the headquarters building.
items.q: What does the label say about the antenna?
o: It is meant for use on land.
It is meant for use on ships.
It can only be used at night.
It is meant for use in space.
items.e: Terrestrial means related to the land or ground.

L: Tell the captain we're all set here; as soon as he gives the word, the convoy can roll out.
o: The convoy is ready to leave.
The convoy needs more time.
The captain has canceled the trip.
The trucks are waiting to be loaded.
items.e: All set means completely prepared, so the convoy can leave when ordered.

L: Corporal Elliott waited at the intersection until the traffic light turned green, then drove on toward the hospital.
o: Where two roads cross
Next to the hospital entrance
At a gas station
In a parking lot
items.e: An intersection is the place where two roads cross.

L: Is Lieutenant Okafor still in her office? I need her signature on this leave request.
Hurry, then. She's about to head out to the airfield for the rest of the day.
items.q: What is Lieutenant Okafor going to do?
o: Leave in a few moments
Return very soon
Cancel her trip
Stay in her office
items.e: Being about to head out means she will leave very soon.

L: Sergeant Mills's sister left the Air Force last year and now works as a commercial pilot, mostly on night flights.
items.q: What does Sergeant Mills's sister do now?
o: She flies for an airline.
She still serves in the Air Force.
She flies only for fun.
She sells small airplanes.
items.e: A commercial pilot flies for an airline, not for the military.

L: Corpsman Neal told the recruits to scrub their hands well before touching any food, not just give them a quick rinse.
items.q: How should the recruits wash their hands?
o: Carefully and completely
With a quick rinse under the tap
Only after they finish eating
Using only cold water
items.e: Well means thoroughly; a quick rinse is not enough.

L: Sergeant Mbeki's unit moves fuel, food, and spare parts by truck and train to every base in the region.
items.q: What kind of work does his unit do?
o: Logistics
Intelligence
Communications
Public relations
items.e: Moving and supplying materials is called logistics.

L: What is the county planning to build on that empty land past the airfield?
A new landfill, I heard. The garbage trucks will start using it next spring.
items.q: What will the site be used for?
o: Getting rid of waste
Producing electricity
Cleaning drinking water
Storing fuel
items.e: A landfill is a place where garbage is dumped and buried.

L: After the parade, the platoon walked to Rosa's Diner, where the owner gives free dessert to anyone in uniform.
items.q: Where do uniformed customers get free dessert?
o: At the restaurant
On the parade ground
In the platoon's barracks
At the owner's house
items.e: Where refers to Rosa's Diner, which is a restaurant.

L: Nobody can remember Airman Fisher ever being absent, not even during last winter's big blizzard.
items.q: What does the speaker say about Airman Fisher?
o: He always shows up for work.
He often arrives late.
He is rarely at his desk.
He works only in good weather.
items.e: Never absent means he is always there.

L: After a visitor slipped on the front steps, the nurse asked the staff to sprinkle salt there before anyone else arrived.
items.q: What was probably wrong with the steps?
o: They were covered in ice.
They were cracked and broken.
They were steep and narrow.
They were crowded with people.
items.e: Salt is spread on steps to melt ice, so the steps were icy.

L: The decision to move the big football game to a weekday evening has split the base, with strong feelings on both sides.
items.q: How can the decision best be described?
o: Highly controversial
Completely routine
Strictly confidential
Very convenient for all
items.e: Strong feelings on both sides make a decision controversial.

L: We can't put off the generator repair any longer; the next storm could cut the power for days.
items.q: What does the speaker say about the repair?
o: It cannot be delayed
It can wait until spring
It was finished yesterday
It costs too much money
items.e: Cannot put off means it must not be delayed.

L: Sergeant Okoro is going to bake several loaves of bread in his own kitchen for Friday's retirement party.
o: Flour and yeast
Wood and nails
Soap and water
Paint and brushes
items.e: Bread is made from flour and yeast.

L: Before the old bridge reopens, an engineer will inspect every beam and bolt for cracks or rust.
o: Look it over carefully
Replace every rusty bolt
Paint the beams and rails
Count the cars that cross
items.e: To inspect something is to examine it closely.

L: The lieutenant stood at the back of the classroom to observe how the new instructor handled the students.
items.q: Why did the lieutenant stand at the back?
o: To watch the teaching
To help with the lesson
To join the class as a student
To answer questions for the group
items.e: To observe means to watch carefully.

L: The hangar where they keep the cargo planes is enormous; you could park ten buses inside it and still have room.
items.q: What does the speaker say about the hangar?
o: It is extremely large
It is older than the others
It stays cold all year
It is crowded with planes
items.e: Enormous means extremely large.

L: How is the new mechanic doing in the motor pool?
Private Owens? His repairs are first-rate; the trucks he fixes never come back.
items.q: What does the man think of Private Owens's work?
o: It is excellent
It is too slow
It is just average
It is often careless
items.e: First-rate means of the best quality.

L: How did the landlord react when you told him about the leak?
He got pretty irked, since I had waited two weeks to tell him.
o: Annoyed
Thankful
Puzzled
Calm
items.e: Irked means annoyed, and he was upset that the problem was reported late.

L: The laundry machines on this floor only take coins. Do you have any quarters?
o: Sure, I have a few right here.
The washers are in the basement.
Yes, they're nearly ten years old.
It takes about an hour to dry.
items.e: Coins pay for the machines, so the reply offers some quarters.

L: The soup in the field kitchen smells wonderful, so everyone is lining up early.
items.q: What can we tell about the soup?
o: Its aroma is very pleasant
Its flavor is very strong
Its color is very bright
Its temperature is very low
items.e: Smells wonderful describes the aroma, not the taste, color or temperature.

L: The temperature fell below freezing overnight, and Airman Cho slipped on the steps outside the dining facility this morning.
items.q: What was the condition of the steps?
o: Slippery because of frozen water
Unsafe because a rail was missing
Too steep to climb safely
Blocked by a fallen branch
items.e: Freezing temperatures make ice, and ice makes steps slippery.

L: The decision to change the dress code has been controversial: some people applaud it, while others are furious.
items.q: What does the speaker say about the decision?
o: It has caused strong disagreement
It has been widely praised
It has not been announced yet
It is very easy to understand
items.e: Controversial means that people strongly disagree about it.

L: Which of the five steps in this repair manual is the main one?
The third. If you skip it, nothing else will work.
items.q: What does the man say about the third step?
o: It matters most.
It takes the longest.
It can be skipped.
It comes last.
items.e: The main step is the most important one; without it nothing else works.

L: Specialist Lowe and Private Pratt are the same size, so they often borrow each other's jackets when it gets cold.
items.q: Why can the two soldiers borrow each other's jackets?
o: The jackets fit both of them.
They both work in the supply room.
They have the same rank.
They bought the jackets together.
items.e: Being the same size means clothes that fit one of them also fit the other.

L: The recreation center on post has a bowling alley, a gym and a movie room, and they're all free for soldiers.
items.q: What can soldiers do at the center?
o: Relax and have fun
Take college classes
Get medical care
Apply for housing
items.e: Recreation means enjoyable activities for free time, such as bowling, exercise and movies.

L: How are you finding the night shifts now that you've been on them for a month?
o: I'm finally used to them
I start at ten tonight
No, I haven't found them yet
The days are getting shorter
items.e: How are you finding them asks how he feels about them; being used to them is a natural answer.

L: Corporal Lee had twelve dollars and I had none, so he gave me six to buy lunch.
items.q: How much money do they have now?
o: The same amount each
Twelve dollars each
Corporal Lee has more
The speaker has more
items.e: Twelve minus six leaves six, so each one has six dollars.

L: The longest river in the world is the Amazon.
I don't think so. Most books say it's the Nile.
o: Geography
History
Literature
Biology
items.e: Rivers and their lengths are a topic of geography.

L: Why did you buy a second alarm clock when you already own one?
o: So I'm sure to wake up for my flight.
At the little shop near the main gate.
Last Friday, right after we had lunch.
For nine dollars, including the tax.
items.e: Why asks for a reason; the first reply gives a purpose, and the others answer where, when and how much.

L: There are no assigned seats on this flight, so the attendant told us to sit wherever we please.
items.q: What did the attendant tell them?
o: They can pick any place to sit.
They must sit in the back rows.
They have to wait for seat numbers.
They may not sit near the exit.
items.e: Sitting wherever you please means choosing any seat.

L: The maintenance crew accomplished everything on the checklist before sunrise, so the helicopter was cleared to fly.
items.q: What did the maintenance crew do?
o: They got every job finished.
They skipped part of the list.
They waited for a new order.
They flew the helicopter home.
items.e: To accomplish a task is to finish it successfully.

L: Please stop apologizing for the mix-up with the leave dates, Sergeant. It's water under the bridge now.
o: The mistake no longer matters.
The mistake was made at a bridge.
The mistake will be punished.
The mistake must be corrected today.
items.e: Water under the bridge is an expression for something in the past that is forgiven and forgotten.

L: Where in the paper can I find yesterday's baseball scores?
o: Try the sports pages.
In the want ads.
On the front page, under the weather.
In the comics section.
items.e: Baseball scores are in the sports section.

L: Do you know who that woman talking to the colonel is?
o: She's our new flight surgeon.
She's talking about the parade.
She's going to the office.
Yes, she gave me one.
items.e: The question asks who she is; the answer gives her job.

L: Sergeant Hill commutes from Arlington, a suburb just outside Washington, every day.
o: Near Washington.
In the center of Washington.
Far from Washington.
Next door to his office.
items.e: A suburb is a town near a big city.

L: The PX has put all its winter coats on sale this week to make room for spring clothing.
o: Cut the prices of winter coats.
Stopped selling winter coats.
Raised the price of spring clothes.
Moved the coats outside.
items.e: Putting things on sale means lowering their prices.

L: Can you read the numbers on that fuse box?
Not a chance. Hand me your flashlight, would you?
items.q: Why can't the woman read the numbers?
o: There isn't enough light.
The numbers are too big.
She lost her glasses.
The box is locked.
items.e: She asks for a flashlight because it is too dark to read.

L: Apart from a short fire drill after lunch, the depot had a perfectly normal day.
items.q: What does the speaker say about the day?
o: It was much like other days.
It was cut short by an emergency.
It was colder than usual.
A large inspection took place.
items.e: A normal day is an ordinary day, like most others.

L: Captain Lopez is a cautious pilot; she checks the forecast three times before she agrees to take off.
items.q: What kind of pilot is Captain Lopez?
o: One who avoids risks
One who loves speed
One who forgets details
One who dislikes the forecast
items.e: Cautious means careful about avoiding danger.

L: Don't try to cross the creek on foot; the current is very swift after last night's rain.
items.q: Why shouldn't the listeners walk across the creek?
o: The water moves very fast.
The creek is far too deep.
The creek is frozen over.
The rain has not stopped.
items.e: Swift means very fast, so the water in the creek moves quickly.

L: These peaches are wonderfully sweet, and they're half price today, so I think I'll pick up another bag.
items.q: What does the woman plan to do?
o: Buy more fruit
Return the fruit she has
Pick peaches from a tree
Cut up the peaches for lunch
items.e: To pick up another bag in a store means to buy one more.

L: A toddler can't cook, get dressed or cross the street alone, so an adult has to stay close by at all times.
items.q: Who needs the most help from other people?
o: A very young child
A truck driver
A mail carrier
A professional diver
items.e: A toddler cannot do everyday tasks alone, so a small child depends on adults the most.

L: The fog was so thick last night that Sergeant Bell could barely see the hood of his own truck.
items.q: What made the drive difficult for Sergeant Bell?
o: He could hardly see the road.
There was heavy traffic.
The road was covered with ice.
His truck had a flat tire.
items.e: Fog so thick that he could barely see his own hood made it hard to see the road.

L: Since we installed double-pane windows, the house stays warm in January, and our heating bill dropped by a third.
items.q: What is the advantage of the new windows?
o: They keep the cold out.
They let in more sunlight.
They make the rooms look bigger.
They are easier to clean.
items.e: The house stays warm and the heating bill dropped, so the windows keep the cold out.

L: Why are you standing in line at the licensing office on your day off?
My driver's license ran out last month, and the late fee goes up every week I wait.
items.q: Why is the man at the licensing office?
o: His permit is no longer valid.
He wants to buy a new car.
He is applying for his first license.
He lost his wallet yesterday.
items.e: His license ran out last month, so it has expired and he must renew it.

L: Is Corporal Shaw coming to the farewell party on Friday?
He was thinking about it, but he finally decided to skip it.
items.q: What did the man say about Corporal Shaw?
o: He won't attend the party.
He will go to the party.
He hasn't decided yet.
He is giving the party.
items.e: To skip a party is not to go to it.
